claims.head: Lohrei and Brunet get the Michkov assignment
claims.call: The Bruins’ P1 (Lohrei and Brunet) spends at least 45% of its 5-on-5 time against the Flyers’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Bruins keep sending Lohrei and Brunet out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Marco Sturm has been picking a defense pair for opponents’ third lines. Tonight the Flyers’ third line is Foerster, Barkey and Michkov.

claims.gist: At home, Marco Sturm likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Flyers’ third line.

claims.head: Where the Flyers have the edge: shots from in close
claims.body: The Flyers are around the middle of the league for shots from in close, and the Bruins are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. Shots from in close tend to be the more dangerous ones.

BOS.head: Anybody’s game
BOS.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Boston has home-ice advantage. The Bruins can tip it if they keep shots to a minimum.

PHI.head: Nothing to separate these two
PHI.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Boston has home-ice advantage. For the Flyers, the difference could be keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: The Flyers need a win

items.text: The Flyers are newly without Cam York and Travis Konecny.
The Bruins are newly without Jonathan Aspirot, and have had to make do without Charlie McAvoy all season.
David Pastrňák is one goal from passing Brad Marchand for fourth on the Bruins’ all-time goals list.
Pavel Zacha is still looking for his first goal of the season.
